assistant:
With the **Bus_28 → Bus_29 [L38]** outage, Bus_29 was just within the voltage limit at 15:00 (0.952 p.u., against 0.950), but fell below it at 18:00 (0.931 p.u.). So the outage was already leaving very little margin at 15:00; by 18:00 the operating conditions pushed the post-outage voltage past the limit.

The main change was higher demand. Demand at Bus_28 and Bus_29 rose from 10.50 MW to 12.77 MW and accounted for 78.4% of the voltage drop between the two post-outage states; Bus_29 itself accounted for most of that local-demand effect. Demand elsewhere rose by 47.25 MW and accounted for another 21.6%. The change in generator output was ruled out as a material cause.

These figures compare the two times **with the same line out**. Measured loads’ reactive demand was inferred at the default 0.95 lagging power factor.

📋 Data source: measurements
